overall: The Board violated the law by posting an insufficiently detailed May 15 executive session notice and by omitting the original posting date and time from the revised May 29 notice; the other allegations were rejected.

allegations.summary: The May 7 notice did not name the individual to be appointed to the Capital Planning Committee.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the chair did not reasonably anticipate that Mr. Ryan would be nominated at the meeting and thus the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by not including his name on the May 7 meeting notice.

allegations.summary: The May 15 notice's executive session topic, contract negotiations, did not identify the non-union personnel being negotiated with.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, we find that the May 15 meeting notice was not sufficiently detailed and should have identified the non-union personnel with whom the Board was negotiating under Purpose 2.

allegations.summary: The May 29 notice's litigation executive session topic did not describe the litigation matter; the Board did not actually deliberate on it.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board did not convene in executive session on May 29 to discuss litigation under Purpose 3, we find no violation with respect to the sufficiency of that executive session topic listed on the notice.

allegations.summary: The amended May 29 notice omitted the date and time the original notice was posted, though the revision fell within 48 hours of the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the amended notice failed to include the date and time of the original posting, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
